name: Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum
description: Beneath the town of Paola in Malta lies the Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum, a prehistoric underground complex carved into soft limestone over several levels. Its chambers and passages were cut by Neolithic people, probably first as a sanctuary and later as a burial place holding the remains of more than 7,000 individuals. It is one of the best preserved relics of Malta's temple-building culture.
